sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Saptasindhu Region
  • Focus on Indus and Saraswati rivers

Deities

  • Indra (250 hymns)
  • Agni (200 hymns)
  • Varuna (Cosmic regulator)

Core Religious Framework

  • Naturalism: Anthropomorphic representation of nature forces.
  • Concept of Rita: The divine law governing the natural and moral world.
  • Sacrificial Cult: Yajna performed for 'Praj' (children) and 'Pashu' (cattle); no priestly class as a rigid hereditary caste initially.
DeityNatureSignificance
IndraPurandaraRain/War
AgniIntermediaryFire/Sacrifice
VarunaRitaCosmic/Moral Order

items.question: Who is the primary guardian of Rta (Cosmic Order)?
items.answer: The god Varuna, who uses spies (Spasa) to monitor human conduct.

items.question: What is the meaning of Max Müller's term 'Henotheism'?
items.answer: Worshipping one supreme god at a time while not denying the existence of others.

items.question: Which Mandala contains the Purusha Sukta varna description?
items.answer: Mandala 10, representing a late addition to the Rigvedic canon.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Avoid projecting later Hindu temple culture onto the Rigvedic period; temple worship was non-existent.
Do not confuse 'Rita' with mere law; it represents the fundamental cosmic order governing the universe.
Rigvedic religion was primarily world-affirming (desiring progeny/cattle), not world-denying (renunciation).

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to early Vedic religion, consider the following statements:
1. It was characterized by naturalistic polytheism and the deification of natural forces.
2. Idol worship and monumental temples were the primary mode of contacting gods.
3. Sacrifices (Yajnas) were performed directly by patriarchs without complex priestly hierarchies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Early Vedic religion completely lacked idol worship and temples (Statement 2 is false).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the deification of natural forces in the Rigveda:
1. Indra was deified as the storm and war god and is addressed in the highest number of hymns.
2. Agni represented the sacrificial fire and acted as the mediator between gods and humans.
3. Varuna was deified as the guardian of Rta, representing the cosmic and moral order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All statements are correct. Indra is thunder god, Agni mediator, Varuna Rta guardian.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to the concept of 'Henotheism' (or Kathenotheism) in Rigvedic religion, which of the following is correct?
opts: It is the belief and worship of one supreme god at a time while addressing hymns, without denying others
It is the rigid belief in a single absolute god that prohibits the existence of any other deity
It is the deification of ancestor spirits as the primary celestial rulers
It is a system that restricts religious practices exclusively to female seers
practiceQuestions.sol: Henotheism refers to worshipping one god at a time as supreme, coined by Max Müller to explain Rigvedic hymn transitions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the early Vedic concept of 'Rta':
1. It represents the natural laws governing the cycles of sun, moon, and seasons.
2. It represents the ethical rules and moral duties governing human behavior.
3. The god Indra was regarded as the primary guardian of Rta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Varuna (not Indra) was the primary guardian of Rta, making Statement 3 incorrect.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Rigvedic funerary practices, which of the following is correct regarding disposal of the dead?
opts: Both cremation (Agni-dagdha) and burial (Anagni-dagdha) were practiced
Cremation was strictly prohibited as it angered the fire god Agni
Burial was restricted to royal chieftains while commoners were cremated
Mummification using herbal extracts was the standard custom
practiceQuestions.sol: Rigvedic people practiced both burning on pyres (cremation) and burying in earth (burial) depending on custom and age.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to the deities of the atmospheric sphere (Antarikshasthana), who is praised as the supreme warrior who destroyed enemy forts?
practiceQuestions.sol: Indra belonged to the aerial/atmospheric sphere and was praised as the fort-destroyer (Purandara).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the early Vedic concept of the afterlife:
1. The soul of the deceased traveled to Pitriloka, ruled by Yama.
2. The doctrine of rebirth (Samsara) was a central element of Rigvedic theology.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Rebirth and Karma doctrines (Statement 2) did not exist in the early Vedic period; they developed in Upanishads.

practiceQuestions.q:
Match the following Rigvedic deities with their respective cosmic spheres:
1. Agni - A. Terrestrial
2. Indra - B. Atmospheric
3. Varuna - C. Celestial
Choose the correct code:
practiceQuestions.sol: Agni is terrestrial, Indra atmospheric, Varuna celestial.

practiceQuestions.q: Which famous philosophical hymn of the Rigveda (Mandala 10) questions the absolute origin of the universe and creator deities?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Nasadiya Sukta is the creation hymn reflecting early philosophical skepticism regarding the origins of the cosmos.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the transition of Vedic religion in the late Rigvedic period:
1. Minor deities like Prajapati and Rudra began to rise in importance.
2. Rituals became simpler and priestly monopolies were dissolved.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Prajapati and Rudra rose. Rituals became more complex and priestly control increased (Statement 2 is false).

practiceQuestions.q: In the Rigvedic pantheon, the deity Agni is addressed as 'mediator' because:
opts: He carries the sacrifices and offerings of humans to the celestial gods
He resolved disputes between rival Aryan clans in the Sabha
He acted as the royal messenger between Rajan and Vrajapati
He was in charge of distributing war spoils in the Vidatha
practiceQuestions.sol: Agni carries offerings placed in the sacrificial fire to other deities, serving as a mediator.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the meaning of the Sanskrit term 'Rtavan' in Rigvedic hymns?
opts: The upholder or guardian of the cosmic order
The priest who performs fire sacrifices
The title of a war chariot commander
The gold neck ornament used in trade
practiceQuestions.sol: Rtavan (or Rtavrih) is the upholder of Rta, heavily applied as an epithet to Varuna.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Rigvedic cosmological system, the sky father deified as one of the oldest gods is:
practiceQuestions.sol: Dyaus (sky father) is deified alongside Prithvi (earth mother) as the oldest couple in Rigvedic hymns.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the goddess 'Ushas' in Rigvedic hymns:
1. She represents the dawn and is celebrated for her brilliant beauty in several hymns.
2. She was praised as a major warrior goddess who led clans to battles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Ushas is dawn goddess. Female deities had no military roles (Statement 2 is false).

practiceQuestions.q: The sacred plant beverage Soma was offered to which god in the highest frequency to secure vitality?
practiceQuestions.sol: Indra was the chief consumer of Soma, which gave him the strength to slay Vritra and fight enemies.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the ethical concept of ' papa' (sin) in Rigvedic religion?
opts: A violation of the natural and moral order of Rta
A failure to pay voluntary Bali taxes to the Rajan
Refusing to participate in military cattle raids
Failing to weave wool garments for the clan
practiceQuestions.sol: Papa (sin) was defined as violating the natural/moral order of Rta, which angered Varuna.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to the deification of forests, which goddess represents the forest spirit in Rigveda?
practiceQuestions.sol: Aranyani is the goddess of the forest and wild environments in Rigvedic hymns.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rigvedic ritual elements:
1. The chants and mantras were compiled in the Samhita collection.
2. The sacrifices were performed using fire altars built inside domestic houses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Mantras were in Samhitas and altars were simple domestic installations.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the term used in the Rigveda for the sacred offering food thrown into Agni during sacrifices?
practiceQuestions.sol: Havis (or Havya) represents the sacrificial offering (ghee, milk, grain) thrown into Agni.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Rigvedic pantheon, the goddess 'Aditi' is celebrated as the:
practiceQuestions.sol: Aditi represents cosmic space and is praised as the mother of major deities (Adityas).

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): Rigvedic religion was primarily this-worldly (utilitarian).
Reason (R): Rigvedic hymns seek worldly prosperity (cattle, sons) rather than liberation from rebirth.
Codes:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Early Vedic religion was utilitarian, focused on cattle, sons, health, and victory, as rebirth/moksha doctrines had not yet developed.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the storm deities (Maruts) in the Rigveda:
1. They were the allies of Indra in his battles against Vritra.
2. They were deified as terrestrial gods of the earth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Maruts were aerial/storm gods who accompanied Indra, not terrestrial (so Statement 2 is false).

practiceQuestions.q: In the Rigvedic religious setup, the solar deity who is invoked in the famous Gayatri Mantra is:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Gayatri Mantra (Mandala 3, composed by Vishvamitra) is dedicated to the solar deity Savitr.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the role of the 'Purohita' in Rigvedic military and political affairs?
opts: Serving as chief counselor and performing rituals to secure victory for the Rajan
Serving as the commander of the chariot wing in battle
Collecting voluntary Bali contributions from the clansmen
Managing the distribution of conquered fields (Kshetra)
practiceQuestions.sol: The Purohita was the royal priest who advised the Rajan and prayed/sacrificed to secure victory in raids.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): Rigvedic deities are primarily natural forces deified.
Reason (R): Rigvedic poets deified lightning, rain, wind, and fire to gain control over their pastoral environment.
Codes:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true. Natural phenomena were deified to seek their favor for pastoral and farming safety.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to the Later Vedic religious changes, the deity Prajapati rose to prominence as:
practiceQuestions.sol: Prajapati (creator) became the supreme god of Later Vedic times, eclipsing Indra and Varuna.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of Rigvedic sacrifices, what does the term 'Yajamana' refer to?
opts: The sponsor or patron who funds and hosts the sacrifice
The chief priest who chants the mantras
The offering item thrown in fire
practiceQuestions.sol: The Yajamana is the host or patron who sponsors the sacrifice to get personal/clan benefits.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rigvedic concept of death and Pitris:
1. Pitris were the ancestral spirits who resided in Pitriloka.
2. Living descendants offered 'Svadha' to feed ancestral spirits during rituals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Pitris resided in Pitriloka, and Svadha was the ritual food offered to them.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following Rigvedic deities represents the supreme sky father deified as the oldest couple with Prithvi?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dyaus (sky father) is deified as the father creator alongside Prithvi.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the term used in Rigvedic hymns to denote the magical or cosmic untruth/chaos that opposes Rta?
practiceQuestions.sol: Anrta refers to chaos, falsehood, or disorder that opposes the cosmic law of Rta.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rigvedic god 'Soma':
1. Soma was deified as the lord of plants and herbs.
2. The entire 9th Mandala of the Rigveda is dedicated to the purification chants of Soma.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Soma was plant god and Mandala 9 contains all Soma hymns.

practiceQuestions.q: In the early Vedic pantheon, the sun deity in his aspect of stimulation and creator is worshipped as:
practiceQuestions.sol: Savitr represents the solar power of stimulation and creation, invoked at sunrise.

practiceQuestions.q: The sacred statement 'Ekam sat vipra bahudha vadanti' appears in which Mandala of the Rigveda?
practiceQuestions.sol: This famous early monistic phrase occurs in Mandala 1 (hymn 164), though often associated with late Rigvedic philosophical additions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the ritual priest 'Hotr' in Rigvedic yajnas:
1. The Hotr was responsible for reciting the hymns of the Rigveda to invoke gods.
2. The Hotr was completely subordinate to Later Vedic priests like Udgatr in this phase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Hotr recited hymns. Udgatr was a Later Vedic priest who chanted Samaveda, which did not dominate in early Rigvedic times (Statement 2 is false).

practiceQuestions.q: The goddess 'Nirrti' in Rigvedic hymns represents which natural/moral state?
practiceQuestions.sol: Nirrti represents decay, destruction, misfortune, and death, acting as the opposite of cosmic order.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the deification of rivers in the Rigveda?
opts: Sarasvati was deified as the goddess of wisdom and speech, and highly praised as a river deity
Ganga was deified as the supreme mother of gods in the early Mandalas
Narmada was deified as the controller of the southern border
Rivers were treated as demons that blocked cattle migrations
practiceQuestions.sol: Sarasvati was the most sacred river in Rigveda, deified as the goddess of intellect and speech.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to the Later Vedic transitions, the deity Rudra transitioned to acquire the traits of which classical Hindu god?
practiceQuestions.sol: Rudra, a minor Rigvedic deity, transitioned to become Shiva (Mahadeva) in Later Vedic and epic times.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the deification of dawn (Ushas) and night (Ratri):
1. Both Ushas and Ratri are deified as sisters who maintain cosmic order in turns.
2. Female deities were completely excluded from any cosmological functions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Ushas and Ratri are sisters maintaining the cosmic order of day and night. Statement 2 is false.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Rigvedic sacrificial rituals, what does the term 'Dakshina' refer to?
opts: The gifts (cattle, horses, gold) given by the Yajamana to the priests
The direction faced by the priest during sacrifices
The south border of the sacrificial fire altar
A voluntary tax paid to the pasture officer
practiceQuestions.sol: Dakshina represents the gifts or fees given by the Yajamana host to priests for conducting rituals.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): Rigvedic religion was primarily non-sacrificial in its early phases.
Reason (R): The early Vedic people invoked deities only through silent contemplation (dhyana) without fire altars.
Codes:
opts: Both A and R are false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are false. Rigvedic religion was heavily sacrificial (Yajna) using fire altars to make physical offerings to deified natural gods.

practiceQuestions.q: In the Rigvedic cosmological setup, the aerial/storm deity who is the companion of Rudra and has his own storm troop is:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Maruts are storm deities who form a troop (Sardha/Gana) and are associated with Rudra and Indra.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following solar deities in the Rigveda is celebrated for taking three cosmic strides to cross the universe?
practiceQuestions.sol: Vishnu is praised in the Rigveda for his three steps (Trivikrama) across the universe, symbolizing solar movement.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the deification of speech in the Rigveda:
1. Speech was deified as the goddess 'Vac' and praised in Mandala 10.
2. Speech was treated as a demon that blocked sacrificial chants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Speech was deified as Vac (Mandala 10). Statement 2 is false.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the Rigvedic concept of 'Anrta'?
opts: It represents chaos, falsehood, and the opposite of the cosmic order Rta
It refers to the copper metal used for fabricating agricultural implements
It was the term for standard barley cakes offered in domestic altars
It designates the chief queen who participated in public sacrifices
practiceQuestions.sol: Anrta refers to chaos/falsehood/moral disorder, which is the direct opposite of Rta.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the term used in the Rigveda for the sacred ritual drink prepared from mountain herbs and purified using wool filters?
practiceQuestions.sol: Soma was prepared from mountain plants and purified using wool filters (Pavitra).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the term 'Rtavan' in relation to Varuna?
opts: He is the upholder and guardian of the cosmic order Rta
He is the chief priest who handles Soma sacrifices
He is the leader of the non-Aryan merchant guild
He is the commander of the war chariot wing
practiceQuestions.sol: Rtavan means protector of Rta, heavily applied to Varuna as the ethical guardian of cosmic law.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to the Later Vedic transitions, the creator deity who became the supreme head of the pantheon, eclipsing Indra, was:
practiceQuestions.sol: Prajapati (creator deity) rose to become the supreme god in Later Vedic literature, overshadowing Indra.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the deification of earth (Prithvi) and sky (Dyaus):
1. They were addressed together as 'Dyavaprithvi', representing the parental couple of the cosmos.
2. Prithvi was praised as a storm deity who accompanied Indra in wars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Dyavaprithvi represents sky and earth as cosmic parents. Prithvi was terrestrial, not storm god (Statement 2 is false).

practiceQuestions.q: The Sanskrit term ' papa' in Rigvedic ethics is often associated with which divine punishment?
opts: Being bound by the noose (pasa) of Varuna
Being expelled from the Samiti assembly
Being forced to work in copper mines
Having cattle herds stolen by the Panis
practiceQuestions.sol: Those who committed sin (papa) by violating Rta were bound by Varuna's noose (pasa), manifesting as dropsy/misfortune.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following represents the primary mode of contacting the gods in early Rigvedic religion?
opts: Sacrificial fire offerings and recited hymns
Constructing brick altars in sacred rivers
practiceQuestions.sol: Invoking deities was done using spoken mantras/hymns and throwing offerings in fire altars.

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to early Vedic religion, consider the following statements:
1. It was characterized by naturalistic polytheism and the deification of natural forces.
2. Idol worship and monumental temples were the primary mode of contacting gods.
3. Sacrifices (Yajnas) were performed directly by patriarchs without complex priestly hierarchies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Early Vedic religion completely lacked idol worship and temples (Statement 2 is false).
mockTestQuestions.q_hi:
प्रारंभिक वैदिक धर्म के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:
1. इसकी विशेषता प्राकृतिक बहुदेववाद और प्राकृतिक शक्तियों का देवत्वकरण थी।
2. देवताओं से संपर्क करने का प्राथमिक माध्यम मूर्तिपूजा और विशाल मंदिर थे।
3. यज्ञ सीधे गृहपतियों द्वारा बिना किसी जटिल पुरोहितीय पदानुक्रम के किए जाते थे।
उपरोक्त कथनों में से कौन से सही हैं?
mockTestQuestions.sol_hi: कथन 1 और 3 सही हैं। प्रारंभिक वैदिक धर्म में मूर्तिपूजा और मंदिरों का पूरी तरह से अभाव था (कथन 2 गलत है)।

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the deification of natural forces in the Rigveda:
1. Indra was deified as the storm and war god and is addressed in the highest number of hymns.
2. Agni represented the sacrificial fire and acted as the mediator between gods and humans.
3. Varuna was deified as the guardian of Rta, representing the cosmic and moral order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All statements are correct. Indra is thunder god, Agni mediator, Varuna Rta guardian.
mockTestQuestions.q_hi:
ऋग्वेद में प्राकृतिक शक्तियों के देवत्वकरण के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:
1. इंद्र को आंधी और युद्ध के देवता के रूप में पूजा जाता था और उन्हें सबसे अधिक भजनों में संबोधित किया गया है।
2. अग्नि यज्ञीय अग्नि का प्रतिनिधित्व करते थे और देवताओं तथा मनुष्यों के बीच मध्यस्थ के रूप में कार्य करते थे।
3. वरुण को ऋत (ब्रह्मांडीय और नैतिक व्यवस्था) के संरक्षक के रूप में पूजा जाता था।
उपरोक्त कथनों में से कौन से सही हैं?
mockTestQuestions.sol_hi: सभी कथन सही हैं। इंद्र वज्र के देवता हैं, अग्नि मध्यस्थ हैं, वरुण ऋत के संरक्षक हैं।

mockTestQuestions.q: With reference to the concept of 'Henotheism' (or Kathenotheism) in Rigvedic religion, which of the following is correct?
opts: It is the belief and worship of one supreme god at a time while addressing hymns, without denying others
It is the rigid belief in a single absolute god that prohibits the existence of any other deity
It is the deification of ancestor spirits as the primary celestial rulers
It is a system that restricts religious practices exclusively to female seers
mockTestQuestions.sol: Henotheism refers to worshipping one god at a time as supreme, coined by Max Müller to explain Rigvedic hymn transitions.
mockTestQuestions.q_hi: ऋग्वैदिक धर्म में 'हेनोथिज्म' (एकेश्वरवाद) की अवधारणा के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा सही है?
opts_hi: यह भजनों को संबोधित करते समय दूसरों को नकारे बिना एक समय में एक ही सर्वोच्च देवता की पूजा करने का विश्वास है
यह एक एकल पूर्ण ईश्वर में दृढ़ विश्वास है जो किसी अन्य देवता के अस्तित्व को प्रतिबंधित करता है
यह पूर्वजों की आत्माओं को प्राथमिक आकाशीय शासकों के रूप में पूजने की प्रथा है
यह एक ऐसी प्रणाली है जो धार्मिक प्रथाओं को विशेष रूप से महिला ऋषियों तक सीमित करती है
mockTestQuestions.sol_hi: हेनोथिज्म का तात्पर्य एक समय में एक ही देवता को सर्वोच्च मानकर पूजा करने से है, जिसे मैक्स मुलर ने ऋग्वैदिक भजनों के बदलावों को समझाने के लिए गढ़ा था।

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the early Vedic concept of 'Rta':
1. It represents the natural laws governing the cycles of sun, moon, and seasons.
2. It represents the ethical rules and moral duties governing human behavior.
3. The god Indra was regarded as the primary guardian of Rta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Varuna (not Indra) was the primary guardian of Rta, making Statement 3 incorrect.
mockTestQuestions.q_hi:
प्रारंभिक वैदिक अवधारणा 'ऋत' के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:
1. यह सूर्य, चंद्रमा और ऋतुओं के चक्र को नियंत्रित करने वाले प्राकृतिक नियमों का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है।
2. यह मानव व्यवहार को नियंत्रित करने वाले नैतिक नियमों और कर्तव्यों का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है।
3. इंद्र को ऋत का प्राथमिक रक्षक माना जाता था।
उपरोक्त कथनों में से कौन से सही हैं?
mockTestQuestions.sol_hi: कथन 1 और 2 सही हैं। वरुण (इंद्र नहीं) ऋत के प्राथमिक संरक्षक थे, जिससे कथन 3 गलत हो जाता है।

mockTestQuestions.q: In the Rigvedic funerary practices, which of the following is correct regarding disposal of the dead?
opts: Both cremation (Agni-dagdha) and burial (Anagni-dagdha) were practiced
Cremation was strictly prohibited as it angered the fire god Agni
Burial was restricted to royal chieftains while commoners were cremated
Mummification using herbal extracts was the standard custom
mockTestQuestions.sol: Rigvedic people practiced both burning on pyres (cremation) and burying in earth (burial) depending on custom and age.
mockTestQuestions.q_hi: ऋग्वैदिक अंतिम संस्कार प्रथाओं में, मृतकों के अंतिम संस्कार के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा सही है?
opts_hi: दाह संस्कार (अग्नि-दग्ध) और दफन संस्कार (अनग्नि-दग्ध) दोनों का अभ्यास किया जाता था
दाह संस्कार सख्त वर्जित था क्योंकि इससे अग्नि देव क्रोधित होते थे
दफन केवल शाही प्रमुखों तक सीमित था जबकि आम लोगों का दाह संस्कार किया जाता था
जड़ी-बूटियों के अर्क का उपयोग करके ममी बनाना मानक प्रथा थी
mockTestQuestions.sol_hi: ऋग्वैदिक लोग प्रथा और आयु के आधार पर चिता पर जलाने (दाह संस्कार) और पृथ्वी में दफनाने (दफन संस्कार) दोनों का अभ्यास करते थे।

mockTestQuestions.q: With reference to the deities of the atmospheric sphere (Antarikshasthana), who is praised as the supreme warrior who destroyed enemy forts?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Indra belonged to the aerial/atmospheric sphere and was praised as the fort-destroyer (Purandara).
mockTestQuestions.q_hi: अंतरिक्षीय क्षेत्र (अंतरिक्षस्थान) के देवताओं के संदर्भ में, किसे शत्रुओं के किलों को नष्ट करने वाले सर्वोच्च योद्धा के रूप में सराहा गया है?
mockTestQuestions.sol_hi: इंद्र अंतरिक्षीय/वायुमंडलीय क्षेत्र से संबंधित थे और उन्हें किलों का संहारक (पुरंदर) कहा गया है।

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the early Vedic concept of the afterlife:
1. The soul of the deceased traveled to Pitriloka, ruled by Yama.
2. The doctrine of rebirth (Samsara) was a central element of Rigvedic theology.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Rebirth and Karma doctrines (Statement 2) did not exist in the early Vedic period; they developed in Upanishads.
mockTestQuestions.q_hi:
परलोक की प्रारंभिक वैदिक अवधारणा के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:
1. मृतक की आत्मा यम द्वारा शासित पितृलोक में जाती थी।
2. पुनर्जन्म का सिद्धांत (संसार) ऋग्वैदिक धर्मशास्त्र का एक केंद्रीय तत्व था।
उपरोक्त कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
mockTestQuestions.sol_hi: कथन 1 सही है। प्रारंभिक वैदिक काल में पुनर्जन्म और कर्म के सिद्धांत (कथन 2) मौजूद नहीं थे; वे उपनिषदों में विकसित हुए।

mockTestQuestions.q:
Match the following Rigvedic deities with their respective cosmic spheres:
1. Agni - A. Terrestrial
2. Indra - B. Atmospheric
3. Varuna - C. Celestial
Choose the correct code:
mockTestQuestions.sol: Agni is terrestrial, Indra atmospheric, Varuna celestial.
mockTestQuestions.q_hi:
निम्नलिखित ऋग्वैदिक देवताओं का उनके संबंधित ब्रह्मांडीय क्षेत्रों से मिलान करें:
1. अग्नि - A. स्थलीय
2. इंद्र - B. अंतरिक्षीय
3. वरुण - C. आकाशीय
सही कोड चुनें:
mockTestQuestions.sol_hi: अग्नि स्थलीय है, इंद्र अंतरिक्षीय हैं, वरुण आकाशीय हैं।

mockTestQuestions.q: Which famous philosophical hymn of the Rigveda (Mandala 10) questions the absolute origin of the universe and creator deities?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Nasadiya Sukta is the creation hymn reflecting early philosophical skepticism regarding the origins of the cosmos.
mockTestQuestions.q_hi: ऋग्वेद का कौन सा प्रसिद्ध दार्शनिक सूक्त (10वां मंडल) ब्रह्मांड की पूर्ण उत्पत्ति और सृष्टिकर्ता देवताओं पर प्रश्न उठाता है?
mockTestQuestions.sol_hi: नासदीय सूक्त सृष्टि का वह भजन है जो ब्रह्मांड की उत्पत्ति के संबंध में प्रारंभिक दार्शनिक संशयवाद को दर्शाता है।

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the transition of Vedic religion in the late Rigvedic period:
1. Minor deities like Prajapati and Rudra began to rise in importance.
2. Rituals became simpler and priestly monopolies were dissolved.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Prajapati and Rudra rose. Rituals became more complex and priestly control increased (Statement 2 is false).
mockTestQuestions.q_hi:
उत्तर ऋग्वैदिक काल में वैदिक धर्म के संक्रमण के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:
1. प्रजापति और रुद्र जैसे छोटे देवताओं के महत्व में वृद्धि होने लगी।
2. अनुष्ठान सरल हो गए और पुरोहितीय एकाधिकार समाप्त हो गए।
उपरोक्त कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
mockTestQuestions.sol_hi: कथन 1 सही है। प्रजापति और रुद्र का उदय हुआ। अनुष्ठान अधिक जटिल हो गए और पुरोहितों का नियंत्रण बढ़ गया (कथन 2 गलत है)।
